questions.stem: Exonic DNA constitutes the coding region of DNA which can be translated into proteins. After the human genome sequencing was finished in 2004 when scientists analyzed the exonic DNA of the human genome it turned out to be which of the following percentage of the entire genome?
questions.solutionHtml:
1.5%

Human genome:

●        Size: 3 billion base pairs

●        Number of genes: <25,000

●        At least 30% of the genome consists of repetitive sequences

●        Alu family constitutes ~10% of the human genome

●        Largest gene: DMD gene coding for dystrophin protein

●        Only around 1.5 % of the human genome is made of protein-coding (exonic) DNA




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 367

questions.stem: Transcription is regulated by transcription factors that either enhance or restrict RNA polymerase access to the promoter. Which of the following prokaryotic transcription factor recognizes the promoter?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sigma

Sigma factor (option D)

  • Recognizes the Pribnow box in Prokaryotes.
  • It forms a complex with RNA polymerase (Five polypeptides – (2 alpha, 1β, 1β’, one sigma) to form the holoenzyme.
  • Different types of subunits recognize different promoters.

questions.stem: The DNA segment from which the primary mRNA transcript is copied or transcribed is called:
questions.solutionHtml:
Template strand

The DNA segment from which the primary mRNA transcript is copied or transcribed is called as Template strand

  • Template strand:
    • Strand which is being acted upon by RNA polymerase.
    • mRNA produced resembles the sequence of the opposite strand (except U in place of T).
    • The opposite strand is known as the coding, sense, or plus strand.

questions.stem: Newly synthesized mRNA undergoes post-transcriptional processing to form mature mRNA. During this processing, the part of the transcribed gene which is retained in the mature mRNA is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Exon

Exons

  • RNA sequences that appear in mature RNAs.

Introns

  • In mRNA encoding genes, exons are often interrupted by long sequences of DNA that neither appear in mature mRNA nor contribute to the genetic information ultimately translated into the amino acid sequence of a protein molecule.
  • These Intervening sequences are called introns.

questions.stem: In eukaryotes, the primary transcripts are processed, and intervening sequences are removed resulting in mRNA and the process is known as splicing. The complex of RNA and nucleoproteins are known as small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particles (snRNPs) perform which of the following function in splicing?

options.label: B
options.text: Facilitate the looping of the two exons into the correct alignment for splicing

questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • In Spliceosomal intron splicing snRNA- small nuclear RNA – U1, U2, U4, U5, and U6 are involved. They remove introns by forming base pairs with the consensus sequences at each end of the intron.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true regarding nucleic acids:

options.label: A
options.text: mRNA is synthesized from the template strand of DNA

options.label: B
options.text: mRNA is synthesized from the non-coding strand of DNA

options.label: C
options.text: tRNA does not contain thymine as one of the pyrimidine bases

options.label: D
options.text: Two strands of DNA are antiparallel

questions.answerText: tRNA does not contain thymine as one of the pyrimidine bases
questions.solutionHtml:
tRNA does not contain thymine as one of the pyrimidine bases

The two strands of the double-helical molecule of DNA possesses

  • Polarity
  • Antiparallel;(one strand runs in the 5′ to 3′ direction and the other in the 3′ to 5′ direction).
  • Genetic information resides in the sequence of nucleotides on DNA strands

Template strand/noncoding strand

  • Strand of DNA that is copied during ribonucleic acid (RNA) synthesis.

Coding strand

  • The opposite strand to one which is copied.
  • Matches the sequence of the RNA transcript that encodes the protein.
  • tRNA is the only RNA that contains thymine as one of the pyrimidine bases. because methylation by S-adenosylmethionine of an UMP of preformed tRNA forms TMP (thymidine monophosphate), which contains ribose rather than deoxyribose.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 355

questions.stem: A 5’-cap is added post-transcriptionally to all eukaryotic mRNAs to provide stability against degradation and create a site for mRNA recognition by transnational machinery. Which of the following statements is not true regarding the 5’ cap of mRNA?

options.label: A
options.text: 5’ terminal of mRNA is capped by 7-methylguanosine triphosphate

options.label: B
options.text: 5’ cap contains 2′-O-methyl ribonucleoside adjacent to it

options.label: C
options.text: Cap is attached to the 5’ end of mRNA through 5’ to 3’ phosphodiester bond

options.label: D
options.text: 7-methylguanosine is attached to mRNA through three intervening phosphate groups

questions.answerText: Cap is attached to the 5’ end of mRNA through 5’ to 3’ phosphodiester bond
questions.solutionHtml:
Cap is attached to the 5’ end of mRNA through 5’ to 3’ phosphodiester bond

Eukaryotic mRNA 5'-Cap

  • The 5′ terminal of eukaryotic mRNA is “capped” by a 7-methylguanosine triphosphate
  • The cap is linked to an adjacent 2′-O-methyl ribonucleoside at its 5′-hydroxyl through the three phosphates.
  • Contain internal 6-methyladenine and 2′-O-ribose-methylated nucleotides.

Post-transcriptional modification of mRNA includes the following:

  • 5' “Capping”: This is the first of the processing reactions for pre-RNA. The cap is a 7-methylguanosine attached “backward” to the 5'-terminal end of the mRNA, forming an unusual 5'→5' triphosphate linkage. The methyl group is donated by SAM (S-Adenosyl Methionine) reaction is catalyzed by the enzyme Guanine-7-Methyl Transferase, which is present in the cytoplasm (rest all post-transcriptional modifications occur in the nucleus).
  • Poly-A tail is added after transcription by the nuclear enzyme, polyadenylate polymerase, using ATP as the substrate. These tails help stabilize the mRNA, facilitate its exit from the nucleus, and aid in translation.
  • Maturation of eukaryotic mRNA usually involves the removal of introns & joining of exons together to form the mature mRNA. The process of removing introns and joining exons is called splicing. snRNA facilitates the removal of introns by forming base pairs with the consensus sequences at each end of the intron.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 400

questions.stem: A scientist has inserted a particular gene in a mouse model and thereafter analyzed the tissue expression of that gene by Northern blot analysis. She observed three positive bands in the lung sample but only one band in all other tissues examined. A possible explanation for this finding is which one of the following?

options.label: B
options.text: Lungs contains three genes for this particular protein

questions.solutionHtml:
Alternative splicing
  • Certain primary transcripts have the capability to be spliced in an alternative fashion, depending on the composition of the spliceosome in the tissues.
  • In this case, the lungs can splice in three ways, creating three different-sized transcripts, whereas all other tissues only splice in one way, creating just a single size of the

questions.stem: The strand of DNA used as the template for transcription has the base sequence GATCTAC. What is the base sequence of RNA product?
questions.solutionHtml:
GUAGAUC
  • Remember when the polarity of a given DNA or RNA strand is not given in question always assume it as a 5' - 3' direction according to the convention.
  • So the given DNA template strand is 5’ GATCTAC 3’.
  • So, the complementary DNA strand will be 3’ CTAGATG 5’. The sequence of RNA formed will be exactly the same as this strand.
  • So Now for RNA, change T to U.
  • So, we get 3’ CUAGAUG 5’. Now in the options, polarity is not given so assume they are asking you for RNA sequence in a 5' - 3' direction.
  • Now we have to arrange the RNA sequence from the 5’ - 3’ direction.
  • So the answer is 5’ GUAGAUC 3’.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 30th Edition, Page No. 361

questions.stem: RNA with catalytic activity are known as Ribozymes. Which of the following is not a feature of the ribozymes but is a feature protein enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
ATP use
  • Substrates of Ribozymes are mostly RNA.  They are mostly catalyzing the synthesis and breakage of phosphodiester bonds. No ATP is used in their reaction

The similarity of Protein enzymes & Ribozymes

  • Specificity
  • Accelerate Rate of Reaction
  • Kinetic Behavior
  • Can be Competitively Inhibited
